Le sujet gagnant répond à trois critères : 1) il vous intéresse vraiment (vous allez le vivre pendant des mois) ; 2) il est travaillable (des sources accessibles : articles de presse française, statistiques INSEE, documentaires, chansons, films) ; 3) il est discutable (une question, pas un thème : « Comment la France commémore-t-elle l'Occupation ? » vaut mieux que « L'Occupation »). Le jury attend au moins deux sources citées avec précision (auteur, date, contenu) — et sanctionne les sujets trop vastes (l'immigration) ou trop étroits (un fait divers sans enjeu). Sujets qui marchent : la mémoire de Vichy (discours de Chirac 1995, films), la musique francophone et les quotas (loi Toubon), la laïcité et le foulard (1989-2010), la famille recomposée (statistiques INSEE), La Haine et les bavures policières. La structure de la présentation : quatre parties en deux minutes. Partie 1 — le sujet et sa raison (environ 20 secondes) : « J'ai choisi d'étudier X parce que… » (la rationale : intérêt personnel, enjeu contemporain, lien avec le programme). Partie 2 — les sources (environ 20 secondes) : « Mes sources principales sont… » (deux sources nommées avec date et nature : un article de Le Monde de 2021, les statistiques de l'INSEE, le documentaire Y). Partie 3 — les résultats (environ 50 secondes) : « Mes recherches montrent que… » (deux ou trois faits précis, chiffres et dates, organisés par connecteurs : d'abord, ensuite, enfin). Partie 4 — l'opinion et l'ouverture (environ 30 secondes) : « À mon avis… / Il est indéniable que… » (un jugement nuancé avec concession : certes… mais) et une question d'ouverture pour inviter la discussion. La discussion : anticiper les questions du jury. Le jury interroge sur quatre axes — préparez-les par avance : 1) les sources (« Pourquoi avez-vous choisi ces sources ? Sont-elles fiables ? ») ; 2) les définitions (« Comment définissez-vous le terme X ? » — préparez la définition de vos mots-clés : laïcité, intégration, résistancialisme) ; 3) les opinions (« Êtes-vous d'accord ? Qu'en pensez-vous ? » — préparez deux jugements nuancés avec concession) ; 4) l'approfondissement (« Et maintenant ? Quelle évolution ? Et en Grande-Bretagne ? » — préparez une comparaison et une perspective d'avenir). La règle d'or : chaque question reçoit une réponse en trois temps (réponse directe → justification avec exemple → relance ou nuance). Ne répondez jamais en une phrase : le jury évalue le développement. La langue de l'IRP : les structures qui rapportent. À placer par cœur : l' opinion (je trouve que, j'estime que, il me semble que, selon moi, de mon point de vue) ; la concession (certes, il est vrai que, toutefois, néanmoins) ; l' hypothèse (il se peut que + subjonctif, je doute que + subjonctif, si + imparfait → conditionnel) ; le passé (les temps composés et l'imparfait pour le contexte historique) ; et la citation (selon les statistiques de l'INSEE, d'après cet article de 2021). Prononciation : le jury sanctionne l'intonation montante, les mots anglais, et la vitesse — parlez lentement, articulez, respirez. IRP modèle : plan complet (sujet : la mémoire de l'Occupation) 1. J'ai choisi d'étudier comment la France commémore l'Occupation parce que c'est un débat vivant et un thème du programme. 2. Mes sources : le discours de Chirac du 16 juillet 1995 au Vél d'Hiv, et le documentaire Le Chagrin et la Pitié d'Ophüls (1969). 3. Mes recherches montrent que la mémoire a changé : d'abord le mythe résistancialiste (toute la France résistante), ensuite la révision historiographique (Paxton, 1972 — Vichy a légiféré seul), enfin la reconnaissance officielle (Chirac, 1995 — la responsabilité de l'État). 4. À mon avis, cette évolution est positive car elle est honnête ; toutefois, la mémoire reste un champ de bataille politique. Question d'ouverture : cette mémoire est-elle transmissible aux générations suivantes ? (Deux minutes, quatre parties, deux sources — le squelette à reproduire.) La logistique : ce que le règlement autorise. Point pratique à vérifier auprès de votre centre : l' accès aux notes (AQA autorise une fiche de préparation limitée pour l'IRP ; Edexcel précise ses propres règles de prise de notes — vérifiez la consigne de votre année) ; le chronométrage (la présentation est chronométrée : deux minutes dépassées ou inachevées coûtent des points d'interaction) ; et la prononciation (les noms propres : Vél d'Hiv, Pétain, laïcité — répétés à voix haute avant l'épreuve). Règle pratique : apprenez le squelette (quatre parties) par cœur, mais pas le texte — le jury reconnaît le texte appris par cœur et le sanctionne en interaction ; apprenez les amorces, improvisez le contenu à partir des amorces. Les sujets d'IRP qui marchent (avec la question qui les porte). Liste testée par l'expérience : 1) la mémoire de Vichy (« Comment la France commémore-t-elle l'Occupation ? » — discours de Chirac 1995, films, historiographie) ; 2) la musique et les quotas (« Les quotas radiophoniques protègent-ils ou figent-ils la musique française ? » — loi Toubon, streaming) ; 3) la laïcité et le foulard (« La laïcité protège-t-elle ou exclut-elle ? » — 1989, 2004, 2010) ; 4) la famille monoparentale (« La monoparentalité est-elle le premier facteur de pauvreté des enfants français ? » — INSEE) ; 5) La Haine et les bavures (« La Haine a-t-il changé quelque chose ? » — Makomé 1993, émeutes 2005) ; 6) l'éducation et l'égalité des chances (« L'école républicaine intègre-t-elle encore ? » — ZEP, carte scolaire). Chaque sujet porte une question : c'est la question qui rend l'IRP discutable — le jury évalue la problématique, pas le thème. La fiabilité des sources : le critère AO4. Le jury interroge systématiquement : « Pourquoi ces sources ? » — la réponse A* distingue trois niveaux de fiabilité : les statistiques officielles (INSEE, ministères — les plus fiables, mais datées) ; la presse (Le Monde, Le Figaro — fiables mais orientées, préparez la nuance : d'après cet article de Le Monde de 2021…) ; et les médias culturels (films, documentaires, chansons — utiles pour l'opinion, moins pour les faits). Règle : deux sources de niveaux différents (une statistique + un article, ou un discours + un film) valent mieux que trois du même type — la diversité des sources est notée. Transition. L'IRP est un exposé : la carte-stimulus est un débat — méthode différente, même langue. C'est l'objet de la section suivante. Ce que c'est. La carte-stimulus est l'autre moitié de l'oral : un court texte (et parfois une image) sur un thème du programme, à analyser et à discuter après environ cinq minutes de préparation. AQA (Paper 3) : une carte, suivie d'une discussion ; Edexcel (Paper 3, Tasks 1 et 2) : deux cartes — une sur les thèmes 1-2 (famille, cyber-société, bénévolat, société diverse), une sur les thèmes 3-4 (immigration, Occupation). La note porte sur : la compréhension (avez-vous compris la carte ?), l' analyse (faites-vous des liens avec le thème ?), l' opinion (devenez-vous un jugement argumenté ?) et l' interaction (répondez-vous au jury, posez-vous des questions ?). La méthode : les cinq minutes de préparation. Utilisez le temps de préparation selon un plan fixe : 1) identifiez le thème (famille ? immigration ? musique ? — écrivez le sous-thème précis : la famille monoparentale, la laïcité, les quotas radiophoniques) ; 2) soulignez les mots-clés de la carte (les chiffres, les dates, les acteurs) ; 3) préparez le trio de base : un fait (ce que dit la carte), une explication (pourquoi), une opinion (à mon avis) ; 4) préparez deux structures complexes : un subjonctif (il se peut que, il faut que) et un si-clause (si + imparfait → conditionnel) ; 5) préparez une question pour le jury (pour relancer l'interaction). Cinq minutes suffisent si le plan est automatique — c'est l'entraînement qui le rend automatique. La réponse : le trio faits-explication-jugement. Chaque réponse à une question du jury suit trois temps : 1) le fait (ce que la carte dit : « D'après la carte, les naissances hors mariage représentent environ 63 %… ») ; 2) l' explication (pourquoi : « Cela s'explique par la normalisation du PACS et l'autonomie des femmes… ») ; 3) le jugement (à mon avis : « À mon avis, cela prouve que la famille se diversifie sans disparaître »). Le jury évalue le développement : une réponse en trois temps vaut trois fois une réponse en un temps. Et l' interaction : relancez (« Qu'en pensez-vous ? / C'est un débat vivant en France, n'est-ce pas ? ») — l'interaction est notée. La spéculation : le subjonctif et le conditionnel. Les questions d'opinion et de futur exigent la spéculation — les structures à placer par cœur : il se peut que + subjonctif (il se peut que la situation change), il est peu probable que + subjonctif, je doute que + subjonctif, il faudrait que + subjonctif ; et le conditionnel de nuance (ce serait une erreur, la France devrait agir) et le si-clause (si le gouvernement agissait, la situation changerait). La spéculation est la marque du registre A* : le jury la valorise systématiquement — deux subjonctifs par carte suffisent. Le registre oral : ce que le jury sanctionne. Les fautes de registre les plus coûteuses : les anglicismes (le film, le job — dites le cinéma, le travail) ; les contractions parlées (chuis, chais — dites je suis, je sais) ; le tu (toujours vous au jury) ; et le vide lexical (les mots anglais, les silences). Les stratégies de survie : la reformulation (si le mot manque, décrivez : c'est un endroit où…, c'est une personne qui…) ; l' exemplification (par exemple, comme…) ; la simplification (si la structure complexe échoue, dites-la simplement mais correctement) ; et les amorcés (d'une part… d'autre part, il est vrai que…) qui gagnent du temps. Règle d'or : une phrase simple correcte vaut mieux qu'une phrase complexe fausse — le jury note l'exactitude, pas l'ambition ratée. La gestion du stress et de l'inconnu. Trois situations à préparer : le mot inconnu dans la carte (devinez par le contexte, utilisez le mot avec précaution ou paraphrasez) ; la question imprévue (gagnez du temps : c'est une question intéressante… puis le trio faits-explication-jugement) ; le blanc (respirez, reformulez : autrement dit…, ce que je veux dire, c'est que…). Et la préparation physique : parlez à voix haute tous les jours (les sujets d'IRP en trois minutes chronométrées), enregistrez-vous (écoutez votre prononciation), et pratiquez le trio avec un partenaire. L'oral se gagne à l'entraînement, pas au talent. Carte-stimulus modèle : réponse structurée (thème : la laïcité) Question : Que pensez-vous de la loi de 2004 sur les signes religieux à l'école ? Réponse en trois temps : Fait — D'après la carte, la loi de 2004 interdit les signes religieux ostensibles dans l'école publique, après l'affaire du foulard de 1989. Explication — Cette loi s'explique par le principe de laïcité (loi de 1905) : l'école doit garantir l'égalité de tous les élèves sans pression religieuse. Jugement — À mon avis, cette loi est défendable car elle protège l'égalité ; toutefois, il se peut qu'elle exclue certaines élèves — il faudrait donc l'appliquer avec nuance. (Trio complet, un subjonctif, un conditionnel, une concession : la structure A*.) La prononciation et la fluidité : ce que le jury entend. Quatre sons qui coûtent des points : le u français (tu, rue — pas too), les nasales (an/en, on/in — distinctes), le r grasseyé, et les liaisons (les_amis, il_y_a — obligatoires). La fluidité : le jury note le débit (ni trop rapide, ni haché), les remplissages français (eh bien, enfin, donc — utilisés en français, pas en anglais) et la gestion des silences (un silence court et maîtrisé vaut mieux qu'un ah um anglais). Stratégie : enregistrez-vous en train de répondre aux questions-types, écoutez, corrigez — cinq minutes par jour pendant trois semaines transforment la prononciation. Et les noms propres du programme : Chanteloup-les-Vignes, Vél d'Hiv, Pétain, laïcité, résistancialisme — répétés à voix haute, car ce sont eux qui hachent le débit le jour J. Les questions-types de la carte : le stock. Les questions qui tombent à chaque carte, par type : description (« Que voyez-vous ? Que dit le texte ? ») ; explication (« Pourquoi cette situation ? Quelle cause ? ») ; opinion (« Qu'en pensez-vous ? Êtes-vous d'accord ? ») ; comparaison (« Et en Grande-Bretagne ? Avez-vous la même situation ? ») ; spéculation (« Qu'est-ce qui va changer ? Quelle évolution ? ») ; personnelle (« Cela vous concerne-t-il ? Avez-vous vécu quelque chose de semblable ? »). Préparez une réponse en trois temps pour chaque type : le trio (fait-explication-jugement) se réutilise à l'infini — c'est l'entraînement du trio qui prépare la carte, pas la carte. Les liens entre carte et IRP : la même langue. Point stratégique : la carte et l'IRP notent la même langue — les structures complexes (subjonctif, conditionnel, passif), les connecteurs (d'abord, en revanche, par conséquent) et le registre soutenu. Conséquence : tout ce que vous préparez pour l'IRP (les jugements nuancés, les comparaisons, les perspectives) sert la carte — et inversement. Règle de révision : préparez trois jugements nuancés par thème (famille, immigration, musique, mémoire) — ils servent les deux épreuves, et tout l'oral devient un exercice unique. Transition. L'oral exige la spontanéité : l'essai exige la structure — connecteurs, plans, registre écrit. C'est l'objet de la section suivante. Le plan : la grammaire de l'essai. Tout essai A-level (AQA Paper 1 : environ 250 mots sur un thème ; AQA Paper 2 : environ 300 mots sur une œuvre ; Edexcel Paper 2 : réponses sur le texte et le film) suit le même squelette en cinq parties : 1) l'introduction (situer : le contexte en une phrase ; définir : le terme clé si nécessaire ; annoncer : la position — jamais un plan détaillé) ; 2) le premier argument (PEA complet : Point, Exemple, Analyse) ; 3) le deuxième argument (PEA) ; 4) le contre-argument (la concession : certes… mais — réfuté) ; 5) la conclusion (la synthèse : peser les deux côtés, juger, ouvrir). Le barème sanctionne l'absence de contre-argument : c'est la partie qui distingue la copie A* de la copie A. L'introduction : les trois phrases. La formule à apprendre : 1) la situation (« Depuis les lois des années 1990, la famille française a profondément changé… ») ; 2) la nuance (« Mais ce changement soulève la question de savoir si… ») ; 3) la position (« Je soutiendrai que la famille n'est pas en crise mais en mutation — pour trois raisons. »). Trois phrases, trois fonctions : le jury note l'introduction en dix secondes — elle doit annoncer, pas raconter. Variante pour les œuvres (texte/film) : situer l'œuvre (auteur, date, contexte), définir l'enjeu (le thème de la question), annoncer la thèse. Le paragraphe : Point-Exemple-Analyse (PEA). La structure de chaque paragraphe : 1) le Point (la thèse du paragraphe en une phrase, avec connecteur : « D'abord, les lois ont libéré la famille… ») ; 2) l' Exemple (la preuve : statistique, citation, séquence, événement daté : « En 2021, environ 209 000 PACS ont été conclus, soit autant que de mariages… ») ; 3) l' Analyse (le lien : « — preuve que le mariage n'est plus le passage obligé du couple, mais une option parmi d'autres. »). Règle : un chiffre ou une citation par paragraphe, jamais une liste ; l'analyse suit immédiatement la preuve — le jury sanctionne la preuve nue. Pour les œuvres : l'exemple est une citation (texte) ou une séquence (film) nommée. La banque de connecteurs : la table. Fonction Connecteurs Séquence d'abord, ensuite, puis, enfin, premièrement, en premier lieu Addition en outre, de plus, par ailleurs, également, aussi Concession certes, il est vrai que, bien que + subjonctif, malgré, sans doute Opposition cependant, néanmoins, toutefois, en revanche, pourtant, or Cause car, en effet, puisque, étant donné que, grâce à, à cause de Conséquence donc, par conséquent, ainsi, c'est pourquoi, d'où Exemple par exemple, notamment, comme l'illustre, à l'instar de Évaluation il est indéniable que, force est de constater, il convient de, il importe de Conclusion en définitive, en conclusion, pour conclure, au total Règle d'usage : au moins un connecteur par phrase de transition, deux par paragraphe maximum ; variez (jamais deux fois donc dans la même copie) ; et le registre : en effet et par conséquent valent plus que à cause de ça et alors. La banque s'apprend par familles de sens, pas par liste alphabétique. Le registre écrit : les structures A*. Les structures qui distinguent la copie A* : 1) le subjonctif placé (bien que ce soit, il faut que, il se peut que) ; 2) le passif (le PACS a été adopté massivement — pour varier les voix) ; 3) les si-clauses (si le gouvernement avait agi, la situation aurait été différente — le conditionnel passé) ; 4) la nominalisation (l'évolution des mœurs — against les mœurs qui évoluent) ; 5) les phrases évaluatives (il est indéniable que, force est de constater que, on ne saurait nier que). Et les pièges à éviter : il y a répété (remplacez par il existe) ; on systématique (variez avec nous, les Français, la société) ; les anglicismes (le film pour le cinéma) ; et le présent unique (variez : passé composé, imparfait, futur, conditionnel — la variété des temps est notée). La conclusion : synthèse et ouverture. La formule : 1) la synthèse (peser les deux côtés : « En définitive, si la famille s'est démultipliée, la souffrance des mères seules reste réelle… ») ; 2) le jugement (la position nuancée : « — ce qui prouve que le problème n'est pas la structure, mais l'inégalité qui la traverse. ») ; 3) l' ouverture (une perspective : « Et si la crise était moins celle de la famille que celle de la société qui l'entoure ? »). La conclusion ne résume pas : elle pèse, juge et ouvre — trois verbes, trois phrases. Le jury note la conclusion en dix secondes : elle doit être la meilleure phrase de la copie. Essay frames prêts à l'emploi (les deux modèles) Modèle thème (famille) : I. Depuis 1965, la famille française a changé… Mais ce changement soulève la question… Je soutiendrai que… II. D'abord, les lois… (PACS, chiffre). III. En outre, les structures… (monoparentales, chiffre). IV. Certes, la souffrance… (pauvreté, chiffre) — mais cela prouve que… V. En définitive, la famille n'est pas en crise mais en mutation… Ouverture. Modèle œuvre (film/texte) : I. La Haine (Kassovitz, 1995) porte la question de… Je soutiendrai que… II. D'abord, la séquence de… (technique). III. En outre, le dialogue… (citation). IV. Certes, on pourrait objecter que… — mais… V. En définitive, l'intention de… Ouverture. Deux squelettes, appris par cœur, couvrent tout l'examen écrit. La longueur et le rythme : ce que le barème compte. Point pratique : à l'AQA (essai d'environ 250 mots en Paper 1 ; environ 300 mots en Paper 2), sous la longueur minimale, la copie plafonne — au-delà, le temps perdu ne rapporte rien. À l'Edexcel (réponses écrites sur le texte et le film), les consignes précisent la longueur attendue — respectez-la. Rythme : trois paragraphes PEA + concession + conclusion = environ 250 mots si chaque PEA tient en 60-70 mots — c'est la discipline qui rapporte : comptez vos paragraphes, pas vos mots. Les erreurs qui coûtent le plus (récapitulatif toutes épreuves). Oral : réponses en une phrase (pas de développement) ; le texte appris par cœur (l'interaction meurt) ; les anglicismes ; le silence non géré. Essai : l'absence de contre-argument ; la preuve nue (chiffre ou citation sans analyse) ; le résumé de l'intrigue (œuvres) ; le registre parlé ; le présent unique. Traduction : le futur après si ; le partitif à la négation ; l'ordre des pronoms. Chaque erreur a une règle — la révision consiste à transformer chaque règle en réflexe. Le calendrier de révision : les quatre semaines. Plan testé : semaine 1 — la langue (les temps, les pronoms, les connecteurs : la grammaire bancaire, un chapitre par jour) ; semaine 2 — les contenus (famille, immigration, musique, mémoire : les chiffres et les dates par fiches) ; semaine 3 — les œuvres (les séquences et les citations de La Haine, les moments et les techniques de No et moi) ; semaine 4 — les automatismes (les trois squelettes : IRP, carte, essai — répétés à voix haute, chronométrés, enregistrés). Règle : la révision orale se fait à voix haute, jamais en silence — l'oral se prépare oralement, l'essai à l'écrit, chaque jour les deux. Bilan. Les compétences d'examen se réduisent à trois automatismes : l'IRP (quatre parties en deux minutes, deux sources, questions anticipées), la carte (le trio faits-explication-jugement, deux subjonctifs, une relance), l'essai (introduction trois phrases, PEA, concession, conclusion trois phrases). Trois automatismes, appris par cœur et entraînés à voix haute, valent plus que tout talent improvisé — c'est la grammaire de la note maximale.

topics.name: Los Cambios en la Familia
topics.subject: spanish
topics.searchText: spanish Spanish Los Cambios en la Familia Describe how Spanish family structures have diversified since 1975, using INE statistics accurately (AQA 3.1.1.1; Edexcel 9SP0 Tema 1A) Explain the legal milestones of marriage and divorce reform from the 1978 Constitution to the laws of 2004-2023 (AO1) Analyse causes and consequences of Spain's low birth rate and ageing population (AO2/AO3) Evaluate gender-role change in law and in practice: employment, domestic labour, corresponsabilidad (AQA 3.1.1.3) Deploy precise Spanish statistics and topic vocabulary in essays and speaking to reach top bands pareja de hecho registered de-facto (unmarried) partnership with partial legal recognition; its growth is key evidence of the decline of traditional marriage tasa de natalidad birth rate; Spain's is among the lowest in the EU (total fertility ≈1,1-1,2 hijos por mujer, INE) hogar unipersonal single-person household; now roughly a quarter of all Spanish homes, driven by ageing and later independent living custodia compartida shared child custody, the fastest-growing custody arrangement after divorce (around 40% of cases) corresponsabilidad equal sharing of domestic and care duties between partners; the A* word for work-life balance debates (AQA 3.1.1.3) violencia de género gender-based violence; targeted by Ley Orgánica 1/2004 with specialised courts and the 016 hotline divorcio exprés the 2005 reform (Ley 15/2005) allowing divorce after three months of separation with no need to prove fault matrimonio igualitario same-sex marriage, legal since Ley 13/2005; Spain was the third country in the world to legislate for it Under Franco, the familia tradicional — Catholic, indissoluble marriage, many children, a male breadwinner and the woman confined to the home — was the only legally and ideologically sanctioned model. Since the 1978 Constitution, which placed marriage outside any single religious framework, Spanish households have diversified faster than almost anywhere in Europe. The familia nuclear (couple with children) remains the most common type, but hogares monoparentales (one parent, overwhelmingly female-headed) account for roughly one in ten families, and parejas de hecho now cover a substantial share of new couples, especially the under-40s. Tasa de natalidad: total fertility of about 1,1-1,2 hijos por mujer — among the lowest in the world; Spain has not reproduced its population since the 1980s. Edad media de la primera madre: over 31 years, one of the highest in Europe; women delay motherhood for career and housing reasons. Nacimientos fuera del matrimonio: nearly half — proof that marriage is no longer the social precondition for a family. Hogares unipersonales: around 25-27% of households; both elderly people living alone and young adults delaying la emancipación . Envejecimiento: more than one fifth of the population is over 65, creating a pension and care burden. For A* answers, always link structure to cause: the housing crash, precarious youth employment ( ninis , temporary contracts), female emancipation and secularisation all push the same direction. Contrast is the examiner's favourite move: antes, la familia extensa era la red de apoyo; hoy siguen existiendo, pero con menos hijos y más abuelos cuidadores. The red de apoyo familiar (grandparents doing childcare) is the survival mechanism that lets Spanish women work — a nuanced point few candidates make. Two structural facts deepen the picture for A*. Familias ensambladas (reconstituted families) are the fastest-growing minority type — second marriages and step-parenting are now normal vocabulary, no se dice «familia rota» . And la emancipación tardía : Spaniards leave home around age 30, several years later than the EU average, because rent outruns youth wages — so the family home absorbs the crisis, sheltering the ninis and delaying both marriage and births. The household count (≈19.4 million, INE) keeps rising even as the population barely grows, because more people live alone. Comparative angle: Spanish cohabitation rates lag France's by decades — Catholic legacy — which is why the pareja de hecho has become the compromise institution. For the exam: use the INE headline figures (fertility, nacimientos extramatrimoniales, hogares unipersonales), then interpret — structure change is a symptom of economy and secularisation, not fashion. One sentence of comparison and one of interpretation converts a descriptive answer into an analytical one. Learn the legal timeline; it converts description into analysis and is exactly what AO1 rewards. Año Medida Efecto 1978 Constitución la familia y el matrimonio quedan fuera del monopolio católico 1981 Ley del divorcio primera ley de divorcio desde 1932; causa necesaria 2004 Ley Orgánica 1/2004 medidas integrales contra la violencia de género 2005 Leyes 13/2005 y 15/2005 matrimonio igualitario; divorcio exprés sin causa ni separación previa 2021 permiso de nacimiento igualado 16 semanas intransferibles para cada progenitor 2023 Ley Trans y reformas autodeterminación de género a partir de los 16 años The data trend: la tasa de nupcialidad has collapsed to about 3 marriages per 1,000 inhabitants — among the lowest in the EU — and civil weddings long ago overtook Catholic ones (over 80% of new marriages are civil). Divorce runs at roughly 85,000-90,000 per year, with custodia compartida awarded in around 40% of cases and rising, evidence of the shift from the mother-default model to shared parenting. Divorce is now cheap, fast and destigmatised: ya no se habla de «familias rotas», sino de «nuevas estructuras familiares» . Top-band answers note the paradox: Spaniards have not abandoned marriage — they marry late, marry less, divorce more easily, and remarry or cohabit. The institution has been democratizada , not destroyed. Anticipate the counter-argument (tradition persists: religious ceremonies retain prestige, and many couples formalise unions only after having children) and rebut it with the INE trend line. The legal patchwork is worth knowing for A*: parejas de hecho are registered regionally with different rights in each comunidad autónoma , and after the 2010 abortion law (12-week framework) and the 2023 reform extending access to 16-year-olds, the family is legislated on from every direction. Las segundas nupcias are common — remarriage normalises familias ensambladas — and the Church has retreated into a niche: Catholic weddings are now mostly a cultural ceremony, and mass attendance is among Europe's lowest. Anticipate the strongest counter-case for the essay: defenders of tradition argue that the divorce revolution has costs — child poverty in single-parent households, custody disputes, and the claim that easy divorce weakened commitment. Rebut with precision: the causation is contested, shared custody is rising, and the alternative to easy divorce is not stable marriage but hidden separation. Quote the reform years (1981, 2005) rather than vague «modern times» — dates are the cheap marks. Gender equality is AQA sub-theme 3.1.1.3 La igualdad de los sexos and threads through Edexcel Tema 1A . Legally, Spain is a European leader: female tasa de actividad has risen from around 27% in 1975 to more than 50%; there are statutory equality plans, parity-driven candidate lists and one of the EU's first consent-based rape laws (2022, ley del solo sí es sí ). Yet the exam rewards the gap between igualdad formal and igualdad real : La brecha salarial remains around 14-15% in average hourly earnings (INE). La doble jornada : women still perform roughly double the housework and care, despite working full-time — la corresponsabilidad is the prescribed remedy. El techo de cristal : women are a minority of executives and boards despite a high share of graduates. La violencia de género persists: hundreds of femicides since official counting began in 2003 keep the issue politically central. The sociological explanation worth citing: under Franco the legal code subordinated married women to husbands ( el permiso marital was abolished only in 1975), so one generation separates legal subordination from today's informal inequality — machismo outlived la ley . The care economy is the A* detail: Spain's welfare state leans on las abuelas , meaning the labour-market revolution was partly subsidised by unpaid female labour of another generation. Build a judgement: Spain legislated faster than it changed habits; the next frontier is el reparto del trabajo doméstico , not rights. Close any essay with a two-sided conclusion — los derechos han avanzado; la mentalidad va más despacio — and quantify at least twice. The legislative milestones complete the picture: Ley 3/2007 for effective equality (pay, boards, plans), the 2010 abortion law and its 2023 reform, and parity — Spain has repeatedly had majority-female governments, a first in Europe and a quick citation for any gender essay. Education is the strongest data point for progress: women are the majority of university students and graduates, which makes the techo de cristal a pipeline question, not a talent question. The ley del solo sí es sí (2022) reframed consent — controversial for its sentencing effects, which gives you a ready-made counter-argument: rights advance, implementation is contested. Build the final judgement in three moves: (1) law leads — four decades of statutes; (2) practice lags — pay, domestic labour, violence; (3) the frontier is la corresponsabilidad , because the care economy still runs on women's unpaid hours. Close: los derechos se conquistan por ley; la igualdad se construye en casa.

topics.name: La Cultura y la Música Hispana
topics.subject: spanish
topics.searchText: spanish Spanish La Cultura y la Música Hispana Explain flamenco's origins and its 2010 UNESCO inscription, and evaluate the folklorisation debate (AQA 3.1.3.2; Edexcel 9SP0 Tema 2B) Assess the global impact of Spanish-language urban music: reggaeton, Despacito, Bad Bunny, Rosalía (AO1/AO2) Evaluate criticisms of reggaeton — misogyny, appropriation, Spanglish — with balanced judgement (AO3) Connect music to regional and national identity in a plurilingual Spain (catalán, euskera, gallego) Use precise cultural vocabulary (palos, duende, fusion, patrimonio inmaterial) in essays and speaking el flamenco gitano-andaluz art form combining cante (song), baile (dance) and toque (guitar); UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage since 2010 los palos the rhythmic styles/genres of flamenco (soleá, bulerías, seguiriya, fandango), each with its own compás (metre) el duende the ineffable state of heightened emotion in flamenco performance; the aesthetic criterion beyond technique el reggaetón urban genre born in Panama and Puerto Rico on the dem bow rhythm; now the dominant sound of Latin pop worldwide la fusión blending of traditional and modern styles — e.g. Rosalía's flamenco-trap — central to the appropriation vs innovation debate la folklorización reducing a living culture to tourist spectacle; the standard criticism of tablao flamenco aimed at visitors el patrimonio cultural inmaterial UNESCO category for living traditions (dance, music, ritual) rather than monuments; flamenco joined it in 2010 las lenguas cooficiales regional languages with equal legal status to castellano in their territories: catalán, euskera, gallego Flamenco was forged in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries in Andalucía — Triana, Jerez, Cádiz — out of the encounter between el pueblo gitano , Andalusian folk song and Moorish inheritance. Its grammar is tripartite — cante, baile, toque — supported by palmas and, since Paco de Lucía imported it from Peru, the cajón . The repertoire is organised in palos (soleá, bulerías, seguiriya, fandango), each defined by its compás . The supreme aesthetic value is el duende : the moment when performance transcends technique — Lorca wrote a lecture on it, a quotation that always impresses. The canonical figures are Camarón de la Isla (voice), Paco de Lucía (guitar) and Enrique Morente (whose experimental Omega opened the door to fusion). In 2010 UNESCO inscribed flamenco on the list of patrimonio cultural inmaterial — state-level recognition that it is Spain's most exported art form alongside the guitar itself. But A* answers need the debate, not the tourist brochure. Critics denounce la folklorización : the tablao circuit performing for foreign diners risks freezing a living art into postcard spectacle, and some regionalists resent flamenco being marketed as la Spanish identity when it is specifically Andalusian and gypsy. The counter-position: fusion (nuevo flamenco, Ketama, Rosalía) proves the tradition is alive precisely because it changes. Structure your judgement as patrimonio vivo vs folclore congelado — flamenco is alive if it keeps evolving. The history deepens with three quotable anchors. The Concurso de Cante Jondo (Granada, 1922), organised by Lorca and Falla, was the first attempt to «save» flamenco from cabaret dilution — proof that the authenticity debate is a century old. The pueblo gitano context matters: flamenco is inseparable from Andalusian gitanos' history of exclusion, which is why appropriation criticism carries moral weight and why crediting gitano artists is the A* move. And geography: the peñas flamencas (local clubs) and tablaos of Seville's Triana and Granada's Sacromonte are the living circuit — the former community-run, the latter tourist-facing, which is exactly the folklorización debate in physical form. For the exam, structure the paragraph as origen → canon → patrimonio → debate : four moves, each with a name (Lorca, Camarón, UNESCO 2010, puristas). Close on the paradox: UNESCO listing protects flamenco and commodifies it simultaneously — a mature judgement in one sentence. After Franco's death, la Movida Madrileña (Alaska, Nacha Pop, and Almodóvar himself as poster designer) made pop music the soundtrack of the new freedom — a perfect link between the dictatorship topic and this one. Spain's pop scene then industrialised (Mecano, Héroes del Silencio), while Latin America produced the global stars: Shakira, Juanes, Maná. The seismic shift is urban music. El reggaetón grew from Panama and Puerto Rico on the dem bow rhythm; Daddy Yankee's Gasolina (2004) made it a genre, and Despacito (Luis Fonsi ft. Daddy Yankee, 2017) became one of the most-viewed videos in YouTube history — evidence that Spanish-language music can top global charts without translating. Bad Bunny has been Spotify's most-streamed artist on the planet in multiple consecutive years, singing exclusively in Spanish. Rosalía is the exam's ideal case study: El Mal Querer (2018) fused flamenco with pop and trap, won Latin Grammys, and MOTOMAMI consolidated her as a global auteur — praised for modernising flamenco, criticised by purists who ask ¿prostituye o renueva la tradición? Her collaborations with gitano and Latin artists are the strongest rebuttal to the appropriation charge. Misoginia: reggaeton lyrics are routinely attacked for objectifying women — quote the term letras machistas . Appropriación cultural: non-gitanos profiting from gitano forms — weigh Rosalía's defence (study, collaboration, credit). Spanglish y globalización: streaming flattened the border between «Spanish» and «Latin» music markets. Essay judgement: globalisation has made Spanish the second most-spoken native language on the planet (≈500 millones de hablantes nativos) and turned its music into soft power — the criticism and the pride coexist. Three more A* anchors. The charts: Spanish-language singles topping the Billboard Hot 100 without translation (Despacito's 16 weeks at number one) — globalisation measured in weeks, not adjectives. The politics of reggaeton: Bad Bunny turned his platform on Puerto Rico's political crisis (2019 protests), showing urban music as protest as well as party — a nuance against the «fiesta vacía» critique. The generational split: parents denounce letras machistas ; their children stream them; the debate is as much generational as moral, which is the mature way to frame it. On Rosalía, complete the case: critics asked ¿prostituye o renueva la tradición? — but the canon itself is fusion (Camarón fused with rock and jazz; the cajón is Peruvian), so «purity» was never the tradition's reality. Judgement sentence: la crítica moral y el consumo global conviven, y la música urbana hispana es a la vez protesta, fiesta y negocio. Spain is plurinational y plurilingüe : alongside castellano, las lenguas cooficiales — catalán, euskera, gallego — each carry musical traditions (rumba catalana, folk gallego with the gaita, Basque rock like Kortatu and Berri Txarrak). This is the substance of AQA sub-theme 3.1.3.2 La identidad regional : music is where regional identity is performed, not just discussed. Festivals are the institutional face: FIB Benicàssim, Primavera Sound and Mad Cool put Spain on the European circuit, while local verbena culture keeps popular celebration alive. Media extend the same story. The telenovela built a shared transatlantic imaginary; streaming has completed it — Netflix's La casa de papel became a global phenomenon in Spanish, and Latin American series now travel both ways. The Latin Grammys institutionalise a pan-Hispanic industry, and platforms mean a Bilbao teenager and a Bogotá teenager share playlists that a generation ago were culturally separate. For the exam, frame the trade-off precisely: Une: a common language market of ~500m natives; artists tour the whole Hispanic world; heritage (flamenco, bolero, salsa) circulates as shared patrimony. Divide o aplana: reggaetón's commercial monoculture can drown regional genres; «hispanidad» marketing can flatten the differences between Seville, San Sebastián and Cusco; the misogyny debate splits audiences by generation and gender. A* move: link this section backwards — the Movida was culture after censorship; reggaetón is culture without borders. Both show Spanish society negotiating its identity through music, first against Franco, now against the homogenising global market. The bullfighting controversy gives this section its sharpest identity example: Catalonia banned los toros (2010, restored on legal grounds 2016), making the corrida the perfect case of identidad regional — one autonomous community's symbol, another's outlawed cruelty. Whether bullfighting is patrimonio or barbarism is a ready-made essay counter-argument: animal-rights movements call it torture; regionalists and traditionalists call it heritage — both positions are quotable and current. On media, add the streaming generation: Spanish-language podcasts and streamers (Ibai Llanos is the reference point) reach tens of millions, extending the same story as Netflix — Spanish content no longer needs translation or validation abroad. Judgement formula: la cultura hispana contemporánea se construye en la tensión entre lo local (lenguas cooficiales, identidades regionales) y lo global (plataformas, mercados) — y esa tensión, no una identidad única, es su verdadera marca. Close any essay linking back: from the Movida's anti-censorship pop to reggaetón's borderless streams, Spanish music keeps redefining identity — first against power, now against algorithms.

topics.name: La Inmigración y el Racismo
topics.subject: spanish
topics.searchText: spanish Spanish La Inmigración y el Racismo Trace Spain's transformation from emigrant to immigrant country, with waves, nationalities and regularisation data (AQA 3.1.2.1; Edexcel 9SP0 Tema 3) Explain the legal framework: Ley de Extranjería, Ibero-American nationality preference, asylum and the Canary routes (AO1) Evaluate integration and convivencia: schooling, labour niches, second generation, El Ejido tensions (AQA 3.1.2.3) Assess racism and antigitanismo with concrete evidence — football cases, hate-crime data, social responses (AQA 3.1.2.2) Construct balanced judgements on whether Spain is a racist society, quantified and rebutted to top-band standard la regularización mass legalisation of undocumented migrants; the 2005 programme processed roughly 700,000 applications la Ley de Extranjería the aliens law (LO 4/2000, reformed 2009) governing residence, work permits and expulsion el saldo migratorio net migration; negative during the 2008-13 crisis, strongly positive since — the key statistic for demographic change la xenofobia hostility toward foreigners as such; distinct from racism, which targets descent — Cortina's aporofobia targets poverty el antigitanismo anti-Gypsyism: structural discrimination against el pueblo gitano, Spain's oldest minority (700,000+ people) la preferencia Iberoamericana nationals of Latin American countries may naturalise after only two years' residence instead of ten las aulas de enlace welcome classrooms that school newly arrived immigrant children in Spanish before mainstream integration la convivencia living together in diversity; AQA sub-theme 3.1.2.3 and the positive term that answers any racism question Until the 1970s Spain exported people: post-war exile (hundreds of thousands after 1939), then labour migration of the 1960s to France, Germany and Switzerland — los años de la emigración that left echoes in the language itself. The reversal is one of modern Spain's defining facts. From the mid-1990s to 2007, the construction and services boom turned Spain into a destination: the largest communities came from Marruecos , Rumanía (the single largest nationality for years), Ecuador, Colombia and Bulgaria. The 2005 regularización legalised roughly 700,000 workers in one stroke — the largest programme in EU history. La crisis de 2008-13 briefly made the saldo migratorio negative — both Spaniards and migrants left; some Latin Americans «returned» to countries that had changed. La recuperación since 2015 restored net inflows: the foreign population now exceeds six million, around 13% of the total — up from under 1% in the 1990s. Venezolanos topped new arrivals in the 2020s, fleeing their country's collapse; Colombia and Morocco remain large. Rutas marítimas: pateras and cayucos to the Canary Islands and the fences of Ceuta and Melilla produced record arrivals in 2023-24 and a recurring political crisis. The legal framework for AO1: the Ley de Extranjería (2000, reformed 2009) governs permits and expulsion; the preferencia Iberoamericana cuts naturalisation from ten years to two — a distinctive fact explaining why Latin Americans integrate into citizenship faster than any other group. Asylum applications surged in the 2020s. Frame the era with the standard essay antithesis: España, que emigró por hambre, se convirtió en país de acogida en una sola generación. Two more data sets complete the AO1 picture. Ucrania: the 2022 invasion brought one of the largest single inflows — over 200,000 Ukrainians under temporary EU protection — and reset the debate about who «deserves» welcome, a contrast the essay can exploit: European Christians received automatic status; African arrivals wait in CAR processing for months. El asilo: applications multiplied in the 2020s (Latin America's crises plus the Ukraine wave), straining a system built for far smaller numbers. Political framing: the Ley de Extranjería is under permanent reform debate — regularisation campaigns ( «regularización ya» , backed by hundreds of organisations in 2024) against hard-line readings — and migration now structures every election. A* synthesis sentence: España pasó de exportar hambre a gestionar la acogida en una generación, y la inmigración dejó de ser tema social para ser tema de Estado. Use the reversibility point: the 2008 crisis showed the flows are not one-way, which undermines any simple «inmigración masiva» narrative. Integration happens in three arenas the examiners expect. En la escuela: aulas de enlace absorb newly arrived children, and the second generation outperforms pessimistic predictions — their Spanish is native, their identity dual. En el trabajo: migrant labour concentrated in la agricultura intensiva (the greenhouses of Almería, the strawberry fields of Huelva), construction during the boom, el servicio doméstico y los cuidados (disproportionately women) and hostelería; remittances sustain entire towns in Latin America. En la cultura: gastronomy, mosques sharing urban space with churches, and mixed neighbourhoods make diversity quotidian. But integration has had stress tests, and citing them is what separates top-band answers: El Ejido (2000) , when riots against Moroccan farmworkers exposed the underbelly of Almería's greenhouse economy; rising xenofobia during the crisis years; and the electoral breakthrough of Vox (2019) campaigning on anti-immigration rhetoric — the first far-right presence in parliament since the Transition, a fact that links this topic directly to the history topic. The conceptual debate is asimilación vs interculturalidad : does Spain demand migrants become culturally Spanish (assimilation, the French model) or build shared space while plural identities persist (interculturality, closer to the Spanish and Canadian experience)? The positive keyword is la convivencia — AQA sub-theme 3.1.2.3 — and it is the term that answers half of all card questions: la convivencia funciona cuando hay igualdad de oportunidades, no solo tolerancia. A* nuance: Latin Americans assimilate linguistically and legally with exceptional speed thanks to the two-year rule; the harder case is cultural and religious difference, and the harder measurement is structural exclusion rather than everyday friendliness. The religious dimension is the integration frontier the examiners probe: Islam is now Spain's second religion (well over two million adherents), mosque-building controversies recur, and the essay question «¿es España capaz de integrar una minoría religiosa?» needs the 1978 answer (freedom of worship, no established church despite nacionalcatolicismo 's legacy) plus the practice gap. The second generation is the strongest evidence of success: Spanish-born, bilingually schooled, legally Spanish by the two-year path, they challenge the very category of «inmigrante» — a mature point: los hijos de inmigrantes no son inmigrantes; son la prueba de que la integración funciona. On the political frame, place Vox comparatively: its anti-immigration rhetoric echoed European far-right parties but won less than France's or Italy's equivalents — Spain's xenophobic vote stayed a minority, quotable evidence against the «racist Spain» thesis. Judgement: convivencia has succeeded where it had money, schools and time — El Ejido showed what happens when agriculture profits without integration; the lesson is structural, not moral. Define your terms before arguing: racismo (discrimination by descent or ethnicity), xenofobia (hostility to the foreign), and aporofobia (Cortina's coinage: rejection of the poor — the most accurate label for much Spanish hostility, since it flares at destitute arrivals rather than wealthy foreigners). The most documented case is football: Samuel Eto'o nearly walked off at Zaragoza in 2006; in May 2023 the racial abuse of Vinícius Júnior at Mestalla became a national and international scandal, followed by the first criminal convictions of fans and by Real Madrid and La Liga formally filing hate-crime complaints — an A* example because it shows both the persistence of racism and a new institutional response. The structural case is el antigitanismo against el pueblo gitano — more than 700,000 people, Spain's oldest minority, absent from school benches and payrolls far beyond their numbers. Hate-crime data (Ministerio del Interior) record well over a thousand incidents a year, with racism the most frequent motive; the Movimiento contra la Intolerancia and SOS Racismo document them annually. The legislative answer includes Article 14 of the Constitution (equality before the law) and the integral equal-treatment law of 2022 ( Ley 15/2022 ). Evidencia de progreso: Spain is statistically less xenophobic than several EU peers; intermarriage and mixed friendship networks are high; the two-year nationality path converts migrants into citizens fast. Evidencia de racismo: football abuse, antigitanismo, labour segregation, Vox's rise. Judgement formula for the essay: España no es una sociedad racista en su vida cotidiana, pero sí en sus estructuras — everyday convivencia coexists with exclusion measured in schools, wages and stadiums. Close by rejecting both complacency and moral panic, and quantify at least once. The institutional response has three layers worth citing in order. Ley: Article 14 CE, the 2022 equal-treatment law and the criminalisation of hate speech — the legal frame exists; enforcement is the gap. Instituciones: La Liga's anti-racism protocol and the security forces' hate-crime units were created because of cases like Vinícius's — scandal producing structure. Sociedad civil: the Movimiento contra la Intolerancia's annual reports and school programmes ( educación en valores ) treat racism as teachable. The audit evidence is the A* differentiator: discrimination testing (paired CVs) repeatedly shows Moroccan or Roma-named applicants get fewer interviews — proof that racism is structural even where the street is friendly. Representation matters too: Afro-Spanish public figures demanding visibility in media and politics show the demand has moved from tolerance to representation. Final judgement, quantified: España tiene menos racismo declarado que varios vecinos europeos, pero sigue teniendo racismo estructural — medido en currículums, en aulas y en gradas.

topics.name: La Guerra Civil y la Dictadura
topics.subject: spanish
topics.searchText: spanish Spanish La Guerra Civil y la Dictadura Explain the causes of the Civil War: Republic reforms, polarisation and the coup of July 1936 (Edexcel 9SP0 Tema 4) Characterise the Franco regime: repression, autarky, the 1959 turn and desarrollismo (AO1/AO2) Describe the Transition 1975-1981: Suárez, the 1978 Constitution, the 23-F coup attempt (AO1) Evaluate the memory debate: pacto del olvido, Ley de Memoria Histórica 2007, Ley de Memoria Democrática 2022 (AO3) Deploy the key dates, names and figures in essays and IRP with top-band precision el Frente Popular the left-wing coalition that won the February 1936 elections; its victory precipitated the military coup los sublevados the insurgent Nationalists of the July 1936 coup (Franco, Mola, Sanjurjo) against the Second Republic las Brigadas Internacionales volunteer units of foreign anti-fascists who fought for the Republic — key evidence of the war's internationalisation el nacionalcatolicismo the fusion of Catholicism and nationalism that defined the Franco regime's ideology and social control el desarrollismo the 1960s growth phase after the 1959 Stabilisation Plan: industrialisation, tourism, urban migration el pacto del olvido the unwritten Transition agreement to prioritise reconciliation over settling Francoist accounts la Ley de la Memoria Histórica the 2007 law recognising Francoist victims, removing Francoist symbols and managing the Valle de los Caídos la Ley de Memoria Democrática the 2022 law declaring Francoist tribunals illegitimate, mandating grave recovery and renaming the Valle de Cuelgamuros The Second Republic (April 1931) promised land reform, a modern army, secular education and autonomy for Catalonia and the Basque Country — reforms that alarmed landowners, the Church and the military while disappointing workers for their slowness. This double pressure produced brutal polarisation: the right's Bienio Negro (1933-35) was answered by the Frente Popular 's February 1936 victory, followed by street violence, church burnings and land seizures. On 17-18 July 1936 part of the army rose: Sanjurjo was the nominal leader, Mola the organiser («El Director») and Franco the commander who emerged from the war as Generalísimo . The war (1936-39) became Europe's rehearsal for its own apocalypse: Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy armed the sublevados (the Condor Legion), the USSR armed the Republic, and the Brigadas Internacionales brought volunteers from over fifty countries. The bombing of Guernica (26 April 1937) by the Condor Legion killed hundreds of civilians and produced Picasso's painting for the Paris Exposition — the single most quotable fact in the topic. The Republic fell when Madrid fell in April 1939 . Balance humano: hundreds of thousands dead from combat, repression and hunger (estimates range from 300,000 to 500,000) and roughly half a million in exile. La «violencia roja» y la «violencia blanca»: both sides killed; A* answers avoid the partisan simplification. La retaguardia: the war's effect on women, hunger and daily life is the Edexcel exam's preferred analytical angle. La internacionalización: Britain and France's No Intervención pact (1936) failed in practice — Hitler and Mussolini ignored it while the democracies enforced it — leaving the Republic isolated; the phrase «¡No pasarán!» (Madrid's resistance slogan) is quotable. Las milicianas: women fought at the start of the war and were then pushed back to nursing and factories — a gender angle that links to the society topic. Los niños de la guerra: evacuated to the USSR, Mexico and Britain, many never returned — exile measured in childhoods. El balance needs honesty: totals are contested (combat, paseos in the rearguard, hunger and disease), so write «cientos de miles» and note the historiographical debate — examiners reward acknowledging uncertainty over inventing precision. Synthesis: the war was simultaneously Spain's civil conflict and Europe's proxy one; both dimensions — social polarisation at home, fascist versus communist intervention abroad — must appear in any top-band cause essay. The regime fused nacionalcatolicismo — Catholicism and nationalism as one ideology — with a single party ( la Falange ), censorship and the abolition of regional rights. The posguerra decades were repressive: executions ran to tens of thousands after the war, prisons overflowed, and hundreds of thousands of exiles never returned. Women's lives were governed by the Sección Femenina : the husband's permission ( permiso marital , abolished only in 1975), no divorce, no contraception, and the ideological equation la mujer en el hogar — a perfect cross-reference to the family topic. Economically the story has two acts. The 1940s were the años del hambre : the failed autarky of a blockaded Spain produced rationing and misery. The 1959 Plan de Estabilización opened the economy; the desarrollismo of the 1960s delivered Western Europe's fastest growth, mass internal migration to Madrid, Barcelona and Bilbao, and the tourism boom that financed the regime. This paradox — repression alongside rising prosperity — is the analytical spine of any Edexcel essay on the dictatorship: the regime survived on material legitimacy, not consent. Oposición: student movement, comisiones obreras , the PCE underground, and ETA (founded 1959), whose campaign dominated the regime's final decades. Valle de los Caídos: inaugurated 1959 by prisoner labour; Franco buried there until his exhumación (October 2019). La sucesión: Juan Carlos de Borbón designated 1969; Franco died 20 November 1975 . La evolución institucional: the Ley de Sucesión (1947) declared Spain a kingdom in waiting with Franco as regent-for-life; the Ley Orgánica del Estado (1966) modernised the façade without sharing power; and the Cortes remained a rubber-stamp chamber — evidence that «authoritarian modernisation» is the right label. The opposition's arc matters: the maquis guerrillas faded by the early 1950s, leaving the PCE's underground networks, student unrest and comisiones obreras as the real challenge — civil society, not armed struggle. The endgame: the assassination of Carrero Blanco (1973, ETA) destroyed Franco's chosen successor and unexpectedly opened the path to Juan Carlos. A* framing: the dictatorship is best analysed as three regimes in one — the repressive 1940s, the autarkic failure, the prosperous 1960s — each with different sources of legitimacy. If your essay says only «repression», you have described one third of the regime. The Transition is Edexcel sub-theme La transición a la democracia and a model of consensus politics. Adolfo Suárez , appointed 1976, legalised parties including the PCE (Holy Saturday 1977 — the regime's own audacious gamble), passed the Ley para la Reforma Política by referendum and won the 1977 elections. The Pactos de la Moncloa (1977) bought social peace with economic sacrifice, and the Constitución de 1978 — approved by nearly 88% — sealed the deal: parliamentary monarchy, regional autonomies, and an amnesty that drew the line. The 23-F coup attempt (1981) , when Colonel Tejero stormed the Congress, proved the democracy's fragility and the King's decisive defence of it. That settlement created the pacto del olvido : no truth commission, no trials, reconciliation first. The debate rumbles on. La Ley de la Memoria Histórica (2007) recognised victims and ordered the removal of Francoist symbols; la exhumación de Franco (2019) and the Ley de Memoria Democrática (2022) went further — declaring Francoist tribunals illegitimate, mandating the census and recovery of mass graves and renaming the Valle de Cuelgamuros . Postura Argumento Defensores del pacto del olvido evitó una nueva guerra civil; la democracia se consolidó «olvidando»; hoy España es estable Críticos (memoria) la justicia pospuesta es justicia negada; las fosas siguen abiertas; las víctimas del franquismo nunca tuvieron tribunal The exam question almost writes itself: ¿la Transición fue un ejemplo de reconciliación o una amnistía impune? The top-band answer holds both: the pact bought stability that generations enjoyed, and the memory laws of 2007-2022 are its moral bill finally coming due. Cite at least three dates and two laws — precision is the mark. Two additions complete the memory debate. The Ley de Amnistía (1977) deserves its own citation: it freed political prisoners of both sides and, in the same breath, shielded Francoist officials — the legal face of the pacto del olvido , and the law the 2022 memory legislation still tiptoes around. Civil society filled the state's silence: the ARMH (Asociación para la Recuperación de la Memoria Histórica) has exhumed mass graves for decades with its own archaeologists and volunteers — evidence that memory from below preceded memory by law. The debate's sharpest formulation: ¿se puede construir democracia sobre una amnistía impuesta por el miedo? Defenders answer that the alternative in 1976 was a second civil war; critics answer that the fear was real precisely because the state never dismantled its own Francoist structures. Exam technique: name both laws (2007, 2022) and both frames (reconciliation vs reparation), then judge with the exhumation of 2019 as your pivot — the moment the pact became unsustainable.

topics.name: Film Study: Volver (Almodóvar, 2006)
topics.subject: spanish
topics.searchText: spanish Spanish Film Study: Volver (Almodóvar, 2006) Summarise Volver's plot accurately in under a minute, using it as evidence rather than narration (AQA 7692/2X; Edexcel 9SP0 Paper 2) Analyse the themes of women, death, family secrets and guilt through named scenes (AO2) Evaluate Almodóvar's technique: colour, camera movement, framing, sound and homage (AO2) Connect the film to its context: post-Franco Spain, La Mancha, Almodóvar's biography (AO1) Build top-band essay paragraphs integrating theme, scene and judgement la madre muerta que vuelve Irene's return after four years supposedly dead — the film's ghost-motif that turns out to be literal el viento the recurring wind of La Mancha, associated with the return of the dead — Almodóvar's magic-realist touch la limpieza de las tumbas the village women's ritual cleaning of graves: death as domestic routine, the film's cultural spine la solidaridad entre mujeres the female network (Raimunda, Paula, Agustina, las vecinas) that does all the film's work — women's solidarity el incesto the buried secret: Raimunda was abused by her own father, and her mother's fire killed him — the film's darkest revelation el congelador del bar the freezer where Raimunda hides Paco's body — the film's black-comedy engine el tango «Volver» the Gardel/Le Pera tango sung by Estrella Morente in the film — the title's double meaning of return el neorrealismo the realist style of hardship and everyday heroism that Almodóvar says inspired Raimunda's character Pedro Almodóvar — born in Calzada de Calatrava , in La Mancha, whose landscapes and women he returns to here — made Volver (2006) at the height of his maturity, with Penélope Cruz (Cannes Best Actress, Oscar-nominated) as Raimunda and Carmen Maura as Irene , the mother thought dead. Almodóvar's biography is examinable context: his post-Franco Movida origins, his matriarchal childhood among women, and his return in this film to the region and the religion of his childhood with affection instead of rebellion. The plot in evidence form: Raimunda's daughter Paula kills her stepfather Paco defending herself from his attempted abuse; Raimunda hides the body in el congelador del bar and takes over the restaurant, cooking for a film crew. Her mother Irene — supposedly dead four years — returns «as a ghost», borne on el viento . The buried secret unwinds: Irene's fire killed Raimunda's father and the lover who had left him (Agustina's mother); Irene then hid for years in the house of the dying aunt Paula. Raimunda was abused by her own father — the incest secret — which explains both her hostility to her mother and the cycle of abuse the film exposes. The resolution: Raimunda tells her daughter the truth ( tu padre está enterrado junto al río ), Irene stays with the cancer-stricken neighbour Agustina , and the household of women closes its own circle. Exam rule: never narrate . Every plot fact must be deployed as evidence inside an argument — la escena del congelador demuestra que Raimunda administra la muerte como administra la vida: con pragmatismo . Plot retelling is the single biggest mark-killer in AQA and Edexcel essays. The film's reception is examinable: it won los Premios Goya (Best Film and Best Actress, 2007) alongside Penélope Cruz's Cannes prize, and it was produced by El Deseo , the company Almodóvar runs with his brother Agustín — the auteur-as-producer model that lets him keep final cut. Carmen Maura carries biographical weight: she was Almodóvar's leading lady in the 1980s ( Pepi, Luci, Bom , 1980) and they did not speak for years; Volver was their reconciliation on screen, so the casting itself is a statement about forgiveness — a detail examiners rarely see and essays rarely miss. Box-office context: a European hit on a modest budget, confirming Almodóvar as Spain's most exportable director. Exam rule extension: attach every production fact to meaning — the El Deseo model explains the film's controlled vision; the Maura reunion explains why Irene's return is written as affection, not reproach. Context earns marks only when it analyses. Las mujeres. The film is a matriarchy: every function — economic (Raimunda's cleaning and restaurant), emotional (Irene's guilt), communal (las vecinas, the tango) — is female, while men are absent, useless or violent (Paco dead, the lecherous bar owner, Rubén away working). The women's solidarity is the film's engine: la solidaridad entre mujeres replaces the family that men have broken. Cruz's Raimunda consciously revives Sophia Loren's neorealist women ( el neorrealismo : hardship and everyday heroism) — a homage worth citing. La muerte. Almodóvar inverts Spanish gravity: the film opens with the village women cleaning graves as domestic routine — la limpieza de las tumbas is closer to housework than to mourning — and treats death as manageable, even domestic (the freezer). The ghost-motif is gentle: Irene returns on the wind, and Agustina sees her dead mother too, so death is a presence, not a void. Yet the film's actual deaths are the darkest — incest, fire, cancer — so the comedy is the surface and the tragedy the structure. Los secretos. The family is held together by what is unsaid; the plot is the slow unsealing of three secrets (Paula's killing, Irene's survival, the incest). The theme maps onto Spanish culture directly: the village that knows everything and says nothing, the graves that are cleaned but not asked about. For the essay, link the three themes into one claim: Volver pregunta qué pasa cuando las mujeres dejan de callar — the moment the women stop keeping the secrets, the cycle of abuse and guilt breaks. That sentence, argued through three scenes, is a top-band thesis. Scene anchors for each theme, named for exam deployment. Mujeres: the bar tango — Raimunda performing «Volver» for the film crew while the village women watch — is the solidarity thesis in one shot: the community that does the film's work applauds its own. Muerte: the opening cemetery sequence contrasts with the film's dark deaths (fire, incest, cancer) — comedy on the surface, tragedy in the structure; Agustina's cancer also carries guilt (Irene's fire killed her mother, and Agustina asks the question no one answers). Secretos: the final riverside confession — Raimunda telling Paula where her father is buried — breaks the cycle: the silence ends with the youngest woman. Class is the bonus theme: Raimunda's informal economy (cleaning offices, the pop-up restaurant) shows post-industrial precarity — la economía sumergida as survival. Comparative point for A*: Volver and Todo sobre mi madre share the matriarchal structure, but here Almodóvar adds reconciliation with the mother — his own biography written into the plot. Almodóvar's technique is highly examinable because it is visible and nameable: El color: the saturated red of Raimunda's clothes, blood and tomatoes — passion, danger and food as the same visual family; the crimson against La Mancha's bare white. La cámara: horizontal tracking shots that move door-to-door through the village like an invisible neighbour; mirrors and frames-within-frames that isolate the women; the famous voyeuristic camera that watches without judging. El sonido: Estrella Morente's tango «Volver» — Gardel's song of return — sung over Raimunda's lipsync; the wind as the dead's arrival; the score's homage to Bernard Herrmann. El montaje circular: the narrative circles back — the film begins with cleaning graves and ends with a grave; begins with a dead mother and ends with a living one. The essay architecture. AQA (7692/2X): one essay, 40 marks — roughly 30 for knowledge and analysis of the film (AO2/AO4 skills: theme, scene, technique, opinion) and 10 for quality of language. Edexcel (9SP0 Paper 2): a 32-mark essay on the film with the same analytical demands. Top-band logic, both boards: Introducción: contexto (Almodóvar, 2006) + tesis de una frase. Párrafos PEA: Punto → Escena nombrada → Análisis (qué demuestra la técnica). Three paragraphs, three scenes, no plot summary. Contraargumento: otra lectura (e.g. ¿la comedia mina la gravedad del incesto?), refutada. Conclusión: juicios matizados, no resumen. Lengua: subjuntivo, condicional, conectores de contraste; citas de la película entrecomilladas. A* move: quote the film in Spanish (e.g. «el viento trae los espíritus» -type scene references) and always attach technique to meaning — la cámara horizontal convierte a la espectadora en vecina: cómplice del silencio del pueblo . Technique refinements for A*: the film's offscreen space matters — key deaths (Paco's stabbing, the fire) happen offscreen or in flashback, keeping the camera's gaze on consequences, not violence; the long takes in the kitchen sequences (the camera moving with Raimunda as she cooks) bind technique to theme — work and death processed in the same domestic space. The lighting separates realism from magic: the village scenes are naturalistically lit, while Irene's appearances glow slightly — the ghost-motif signalled by light, not effects. The score's Herrmann homage (Almodóvar's tribute to Hitchcock's Vertigo ) places the film in the melodrama tradition. Essay technique: match the command word — «analiza» demands technique-plus-meaning; «hasta qué punto» demands a scale; «compara» demands parallel structure across both films. And always quote the film in Spanish with the scene named ( «la escena del tango en el bar» ): named scenes + quoted Spanish + meaning = the three ingredients every top-band paragraph shares.

topics.name: Film Study: Ocho Apellidos Vascos (2014)
topics.subject: spanish
topics.searchText: spanish Spanish Film Study: Ocho Apellidos Vascos (2014) Summarise the plot accurately and evaluate its record-breaking commercial success (AQA 7692/2X; Edexcel 9SP0 Paper 2) Analyse identity as performance: the invented Basque identity and the double stereotypes mocked (AO2) Evaluate comedy's function in a nation still negotiating its past (post-ETA context) (AO2/AO3) Assess technique: dialect humour, contrasting spaces, casting and genre hybridity (AO2) Compare OAV with Volver: same themes, opposite tone — a ready-made essay structure el estereotipo regional the simplified national caricature (the lazy, partying Andalusian; the dour, nationalist Basque) the film plays with and dismantles la identidad como performance identity as something learned and performed: Rafa's fake Basque self, «Antón Goienetxeberria», built from lessons and costume el zulo the hideout (a Basque word) where the fugitive father Koldo lives beneath the house — the film's political wink el euskera the Basque language, the film's central comic device and the marker of a real identity Rafa cannot fake la reconciliación the post-ETA, post-crisis mood of 2011-14 the film channels: laughing at division instead of fighting over it la taquilla the box office; OAV's ~9.5m admissions made it Spain's most-seen Spanish film of its era el propio género de comedia romántica the romantic-comedy framework (chance meeting, false pretences, reunion) that carries the political satire el estereotipo invertido the twist that undermines the stereotype — the family's own «Basque purity» turns out to be partly Andalusian Emilio Martínez-Lázaro — veteran of Spanish romantic comedy ( El otro lado de la cama ) — released Ocho Apellidos Vascos in 2014 into a very specific mood: Spain deep in the post-2008 crisis, ETA's definitive ceasefire announced (2011) and its disbandment approaching (2018), and a public exhausted by political division. The film answered with escapism — and became a phenomenon: roughly 9.5 millones de espectadores and more than €50m at la taquilla , the most-seen Spanish film of its generation, with a sequel ( Ocho Apellidos Catalanes , 2015) that imported the 2017 independence tensions before they happened. Lead casting was comedy-native: Dani Rovira (breakthrough role), Clara Lago , Karra Elejalde and Carmen Machi . The plot in evidence form: Rafa , a cartoonishly Sevillian hairdresser who has never left his barrio, meets Amaia , a Basque woman on her hen night in Seville; after one night she vanishes, leaving her handbag. Rafa travels to Getaria (Gipuzkoa) to return it, falls for her, and to win over her hostile father pretends to be Basque under the invented identity «Antón Goienetxeberria» — learning euskera phonetics, donning the beret and performing every stereotype available. The farce escalates: the father Koldo turns out to be a preso fugado living hidden in a zulo beneath the house; a wedding is planned on the fake identity; Rafa's act collapses and both men end up in Seville; the film ends with reunion and the twist that the family's «Basque purity» is partly Andalusian after all. Exam rule as with Volver: never narrate — deploy plot as evidence. The record-breaking taquilla figure is itself evidence: a wounded, broke, post-ETA Spain chose to laugh at its own divisions rather than fight about them. Commercial context for A*: OAV broke the Spanish record held by Torrente 4 (2011) and became the benchmark for home-grown comedy — proof that a domestic film can beat Hollywood imports on home soil. Its success was structural as much as comic: the 2008-13 crisis had crushed cinema attendance, and the film's cheap, sunny escapism met a country that wanted to laugh. Production context: Lazona Films with Telecinco Cinema — television money, broad casting, maximum accessibility — the opposite of Almodóvar's auteur model, itself a comparison point: two Spanish cinemas, one commercial, one personal, both successful. Martínez-Lázaro's CV matters: El otro lado de la cama (2002) had already defined the Spanish romantic comedy of the 2000s, and OAV extended its formula — musical numbers out, regional stereotypes in. Exam rule: the taquilla figure is evidence of a national mood, not a quality judgement; use it to explain why the film resonated (post-ETA, crisis, exhaustion with division), and let the scenes carry the analysis. La identidad como performance. The film's deepest joke: Basque identity — the most defended identity in Spain — can be faked with a beret, phonetics and enthusiasm, which suggests identity is learned behaviour, not blood. Rafa invents Antón from a handful of lessons; the neighbours accept him. The title is the thesis: ocho apellidos vascos — lineage as identity — and the film spends two hours proving lineage proves nothing. The twist completes it: the family's own purity myth collapses when an elder relative turns out to be Andalusian. For essays, the claim is ready-made: la película desmonta la idea de una identidad «pura» mostrando que toda identidad se aprende y se actúa . Los estereotipos dobles. The film mocks in both directions, and that symmetry is its defence against accusations of mockery: El andaluz: Rafa — seductive, work-shy, fiesta-obsessed, trapped in his barrio; every cliché of the south. El vasco: dour, closed, eternally ready to be offended, obsessed with purity of lineage; every cliché of the north. La función: laughing at both stereotypes disarms both; the romance between Rafa and Amaia literally crosses the caricature divide, and her falling for the fake Basque proves the person matters more than the label. The exam question «¿se ríe la película DE los estereotipos o CON ellos?» answers itself: los dos — and the second half of the sentence is the analytical point: by laughing with both sides at both sides, the film does the opposite of dividing; it performs la reconciliación . Cite the post-ETA context: in 2014 the nation could finally laugh at what it had feared for forty years. Compare directly with Volver : the same materials — women, family, regional identity, secrets — treated as drama by Almodóvar and as farce by Martínez-Lázaro; the contrast is a complete essay architecture for both films. Two refinements. The depoliticisation point: the film pointedly keeps Koldo's crime vague — a fugitive, yes, but the script never says ETA — so the comedy laughs at regional difference while carefully avoiding terrorism; that restraint is why it played in both Bilbao and Seville. A* essays can note the irony: the most charged identity conflict of the era is handled by a film that never names it, and the laughter works because the wound is given space to heal. Self-deprecation: the Andalusian stereotype is written with Andalusian sensibility — Rafa is the film's heart, and southern audiences laughed with him, not at him; the joke's direction matters, and the film is careful that every caricature has a sympathetic face. Identity conclusion, restated at essay depth: la película demuestra que la identidad nacional española se construye en la burla mutua entre regiones — y que la única identidad «pura» es la que uno se inventa. The title's eight surnames are the thesis: lineage is where identity starts, and the film proves it is where it ends. The technique is built on contrast, and each contrast is nameable: El contraste de espacios: sun-saturated, claustrophobic Seville (one bar, one street, one barrio) against the open Atlantic coast of Getaria — south and north as visual characters. El contraste lingüístico: the euskera gag — Rafa treating an unpronounceable language as a magic password — is the film's most-quoted device and its sharpest point: language is the identity marker no costume can fake. El contraste musical y de vestuario: flamenco-pop Southern soundtrack and Rafa's Sevillian finery against the austere northern setting — stereotype as costume design. El ritmo del género: slapstick escalation plus romantic-comedy structure (chance meeting, false pretences, confession, reunion) carrying political satire — the hybridity is the point. The essay architecture (same marks as Volver: AQA 40, Edexcel 32): introducción with context (2014, post-ETA, taquilla) + one-sentence thesis; PEA paragraphs each fusing a scene to a claim (the identity-lesson scenes → identity as performance; the Koldo zulo scenes → the political wink; the wedding farce → purity myth dismantled); a counter-argument (does laughing at stereotypes reinforce them? answered by the film's double-direction mockery and the romance that crosses the divide); a matizada conclusion; subjunctive and contrast connectors throughout. A* move: name the genre theorists' instinct without naming theorists — la comedia permite hablar de lo que el drama no puede — and, as with Volver, quote dialogue briefly: the invented surname itself is the best quotation in the film. Two technique refinements. The dialect gag structure: the euskera jokes work by a repeated mechanism — a foreign, unpronounceable language treated as a password — and the film varies the mechanism (learning phonetics, mispronouncing, deploying it at the wedding), which is worth noting: good comedy repeats with variation, and the exam rewards seeing the structure. The soundtrack's contrast: flamenco-flavoured southern pop against the northern austerity — sound as costume, reinforcing the visual stereotypes; and the comic timing of the slapstick (the chase sequences, the wedding collapse) sits against quiet two-shots between Rafa and Amaia, where the romance breathes — the genre hybridity is audible as well as visible. Comparison move for the exam: prepare one paragraph pairing the two set films on technique — Almodóvar's controlled frames and offscreen violence versus Martínez-Lázaro's kinetic farce and onscreen absurdity — same themes, opposite cameras. Close the essay on function: la comedia no evita el tema nacional; lo hace soportable — and the film's reception in both regions is the proof.

topics.name: Grammar Bank
topics.subject: spanish
